summary: Routing mistakes are often silent: an easy-looking request can be the dangerous one, and an early low-quality artifact can anchor every later stage. Cascades also add tail latency and a new control-plane dependency.

points.text: A false-negative trigger returns the cheap model's wrong answer without escalation. Average benchmark quality can hide rare, high-cost routing misses.
Passing the first model's plan or answer to a stronger model creates anchoring and shared-context error; escalation may polish rather than independently reassess the result.
Multiple sequential calls worsen tail latency and may exceed the cost of calling the stronger model once for tasks that frequently escalate.
Provider fallbacks can change tool support, context limits, privacy jurisdiction, safety behavior, and output semantics. Availability is not semantic equivalence.
